bullets: Un sistema rápido cruza el lunes con humedad y dinámica limitadas: solo chubascos ligeros y acumulaciones mínimas en terreno alto.
Una cresta de alta presión trae tiempo seco desde el martes hasta al menos media semana.
Para Thanksgiving y el fin de semana sigue posible un patrón más activo, pero los ensambles no coinciden (confianza baja).

sections.Key Messages:
- Snow will begin along the northern Divide late Friday,
  lingering through Sunday morning. Snow totals of 10-14 inches
  are expected for the Park and Elkhead mountains, with 4-8
  inches across the Flat Tops and Central Divide Mountains.
- Winds gusting up to 45 mph are expected with this evening,
  leading to blowing and drifting snow and difficult driving
  conditions over the mountain passes.
- An unsettled pattern looks to continue into next week with potential
  for more mountain snow, but details remain uncertain.
sections.Discussion:
Issued at 1039 PM MST Thu Nov 26 2026
QUIET THROUGH FRIDAY EVENING
The ridge to our west is in the process of breaking down this
evening, with increasing upper level moisture in the form of mid to
high level clouds spilling in from the northwest. Aside from the
clouds, seasonably mild temperatures and relatively quiet conditions
will continue through the day Friday.
SNOWY INTO THE WEEKEND
The first in a series of shortwaves in the northwesterly flow
reaches eastern Utah and western Colorado Friday evening. Light snow
showers are expected to begin along the Northern Divide and spread
south through the night. The strongest in this series of waves
arrives Saturday morning, with the highest snowfall rates expected
between 5AM and 5PM Saturday. This will impact morning and evening
commutes, as well as any post-Thanksgiving Holiday traffic over the
mountain passes. A Winter Storm Warning has been issued for the Park
and Elkhead mountains, and Winter Weather Advisories remain in
effect for the Central Divide mountains and Flat Tops, all from 5PM
Friday evening to 5AM Sunday morning. For the Park and Elkhead
mountains, 10-14 inches of snow are expected, with locally higher
amounts possible. For the Central Divide Mountains and the Flat
Tops, snow totals of 4-8 inches are expected, with locally higher
amounts possible. This system will also bring strong northwesterly
winds capable of gusting to 45 mph. As a result, blowing and
drifting snow will also be a concern. If planning on travelling at
any point on Saturday, be prepared for difficult winter driving
conditions, with blowing snow reducing visibility and slick, messy
road conditions.
SUNDAY AND BEYOND
Snow showers will taper off Sunday morning, with only a few
orographically driven showers lingering along the Park Range under
drying northwesterly flow. A transient ridge builds in Sunday into
Monday, bringing quieter conditions seasonably mild temperatures.
This ridge flattens through the day Monday, with flow shifting from
northwesterly to more zonal in response to a wave moving into the
Pacific Northwest. Model confidence with the impact of this first
wave remains low, however it is possible that increasing moisture
and favorable orographics will result in some light snow showers
along the Divide. Blended guidance has reasonably high probabilities
(50-70%) of an inch or two of snow with this first wave. Looking
towards the middle of the week, there is potential for a stronger,
more southerly system to impact the Four Corners and southern
mountains. Model guidance remains in relatively poor agreement, with
significant spread. The southerly track does increase potential for
atmospheric river moisture to accompany this system. However, the
exact track of this system can make the difference between a solid
mountain snowfall and seeing no snow at all. We shall have to wait
and see how the forecast for this system develops over the coming
days.
sections.Aviation:
Issued at 416 AM MST Fri Nov 27 2026
Scattered to broken high clouds will continue moving into the
area today. Some midlevel ceilings at KHDN and KEGE are being
reported attm but should not persist too long once the sun comes
up. Clouds will start to lower and thicken in the afternoon and
evening hours with some precip possible towards the end of the
TAF period. Having said that, KHDN may see some light precip
after 00Z. VFR conditions will remain predominant.
